session.title: rn that achieves a purpose from a request alone

goals.what: Whoever wants to hand a whole piece of work to an agent asks for it without preparing anything, only answers what they are asked, and their purpose is achieved; rn 0.10.0 brings this to them.
goals.why: Work that takes days then reaches a merged result with the user called only for their own decisions, deciding each sign-off from the proposal alone and going on from the record the next day, as issue #54 says.

acceptance_criteria.what: On real requests, the user sends back few changes at the deliverable sign-off, none once G1 is reached.
On the same requests, the user spends little time from asking to their purpose achieved, with AC1 no worse.

tasks.what: lane holds a plugin's flow: the plugin declares the order its roles go in, and lane gives each next move and holds the orchestrator to it

completion_criteria.what: lane's README, UX and architecture promise and design the flow, each passing its template's questions and agreed by the user
lane depends on no plugin: no code, document or example of it names turn, rn or another ccpm plugin
check.sh lane 100%, mutate.sh lane 0 survivors, and its trials passing

tasks.what: Pin, a plugin of its own in ccpm, pins a plan down from its purpose: a design tree from the goal down, the user asked only what is theirs, one point at a time, nothing left assumed; Turn and rn take it in by dependencies

completion_criteria.what: Pin's skill, pin:down, made from Matt Pocock's grilling skill (MIT, credited) and turn-rebuild.md's Design tree, and its script checking a design-tree.json: every question served, every decision reaching the root, the order following builds_on
tried first: a role of Turn runs the script of Pin, its dependency, and Lane checks that call; if it cannot, where the script lies is decided again
Pin is built by .claude/rules/dev.md: check.sh Pin 100%, mutate.sh Pin 0 survivors, and its trials passing

tasks.what: turn rebuilt on the concept and roles agreed in turn-rebuild.md

completion_criteria.what: turn's UX, README and architecture are rewritten from turn-rebuild.md and agreed by the user, each written after its kind's template, the Format and the Checklist, is remade by planner's steps and the user has approved the kind's purpose and conditions.
turn's code, with its comments and docstrings, is written after the code template is remade the same way, and passes its questions
turn is built by .claude/rules/dev.md: check.sh turn 100%, mutate.sh turn 0 survivors, and its acceptance trials passing

released on the user's instruction, the branch merged once Turn is rebuilt

completion_criteria.what: Each template holds a kind's Format and Checklist in JSON, and the user approved each kind's purpose and conditions

tasks.what: rn remade on T41's turn: it carries a run over many turns without drift to a work of value to the user, by grilling the user down a design tree and by ACC, keeping its state compressed from move to move, and calls turn for each work

completion_criteria.what: A request in rough words reaches the plan sign-off with the user asked only the points that are theirs, one per message
The user approves each sign-off from the proposal alone, and meets at the deliverable sign-off a finished work that does every acceptance criterion
The steering holds only what is left and where the session stands, replanned from each move's facts; check.sh rn 100%, mutate.sh rn 0 survivors
rn's UX, README, architecture and the comments and docstrings of its code pass their templates' questions
rn's commands named again from what each does once rebuilt, as rn:gm, which sends back feedback, reads as good morning (the user, 2026-11-03: names fit each command's essence, not one another)

rn's prompts hold the steps of writing an issue and a pull request and of the check before a pull request is marked ready, and .claude/rules/issue.md and final-check.md point to them, keeping only ccpm's own (the user, 2026-11-04)
